# Rendered by _work/scripts/S_90_terms.py render. Lines starting with # are comments.

column3: Confirmed: the statement was read directly in code or `data/` at commit `f909630` and is cited as `path:Symbol`.
Inferred: derived from confirmed facts by stated reasoning (arithmetic, absence of callers, reachability); never presented as read directly.
Unknown: the source tree cannot settle the point; every such item is numbered NN-U<n> in its document's "Open questions and unknowns" with what would resolve it.
Present and reachable in the baseline build: `Release|Win32` (OpenGL) with `TARGET_PC_FULLGAME`, shipped as `multiwinia.exe`.
Only in the secondary `ReleaseDirect3D` configuration (`USE_DIRECT3D`), where a Direct3D 9 layer emulates the OpenGL API; [I] probably does not compile at this commit.
Only under `TARGET_DEBUG` (cheat menu, sound and gesture editors, `TRACK_SYNC_RAND`, Tank Battle, The Beast crate).
Only under `LOCATION_EDITOR`, which every shipped target leaves commented out: the in-game map editor and its windows.
Restricted by the demo gate: either the runtime check `IS_DEMO` (no valid full-version key) inside the full build, or the separate `TARGET_MULTIWINIA_DEMOONLY` product target; each use states which.
Compiled into the full build but unreachable in Multiwinia: Darwinia campaign code, objects blocked by `BLOCK_OLD_DARWINIA_OBJECTS`, single-player-only branches.
Not compiled in any PC configuration (macro never defined, file excluded, or platform-only); documented only in appendices.

The two developer configurations (`darwinia_d_gl.exe`, `darwinia_d.exe`); unrelated to the `TARGET_DEBUG` product target, which is a separate source switch.
The single active product target in `code/lib/universal_include.h`; it enables LAN/WAN play, all six shipped modes, basic and advanced crates, the tutorial and `BLOCK_OLD_DARWINIA_OBJECTS`.
Developer product target: adds Tank Battle, Prologue/Campaign menu entries, the cheat menu, sound and gesture editors, AVI capture, `TRACK_SYNC_RAND` and The Beast crate. Source of [B:DEBUG].

`TARGET_PC_PREVIEW`, `TARGET_PC_HARDWARECOMPAT`, `TARGET_ASSAULT_STRESSTEST`, `TARGET_BETATEST_GROUP_ALL`, `TARGET_BETATEST_GROUP_A/B/C`: commented-out targets that restrict modes, crates and `PERMITTED_MAPS` for previews, hardware tests, stress tests and beta groups.

On in FULLGAME: `Building::BuildingIsBlocked` and `Entity::EntityIsBlocked` refuse level-file placement of Darwinia-only types (39 building types, the blocked entity types). Code can still create them at run time.

Set by `Direct3D.vsprops`; replaces native OpenGL with the `code/lib/opengl_directx*` emulation layer over Direct3D 9.
Never defined: gates the Darwinia mentor, help system and tutorial code (49 files), all [B:DEAD].
Never defined: automated two-machine test bed with `testbedconfig.txt`; also stretches `GRACE_TIME` to 20 s.

Global switch that makes SystemIV's `Fixed` numeric type a wrapper around `double`; the fixed-point alternatives `USE_FIXED` and `FIXED64_NUMERICS` are never defined.
Global crash-report hook (structured-exception report and support tool) and the switch that writes `debug.txt`; DUMP_DEBUG_LOG is on in FULLGAME.

Commented out: gates the boot-loader mini-programs and the first-time start sequence, so they are [B:DEAD].
Set to 1 in FULLGAME: the server removes any remote client whose authentication-key check fails (`Server::AuthenticateClients`).
Defined in `code/deform.cpp`; selects the StretchRect capture path of the [B:D3D] deform effect, which makes its pre-render `Start()` a no-op (source comment: it "should make FSAA possible").
Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release: the four-stage volume envelope a sound instance applies over its playback.
Artificial intelligence; in this set usually the CPU player, which is the entity class `AI` (one per CPU team) driving that team's officers, tasks and crowds. See `AI` entity.
Network data-field code `dg` carrying a packed `TeamControls` record, the continuous per-team input sent every frame.
Application programming interface.
OpenGL extension-family prefix (Architecture Review Board), the Windows OpenGL binding layer, and the OpenGL utility library; all three are used by the native renderer.
7-bit character encoding; most data text files are ASCII or 8-bit, widened byte-for-byte to Unicode on load.
Short mode tokens used in tables: Assault, Domination, Rocket Riot, Blitzkrieg, Tank Battle (with KOTH and CTS).
column5: yes → Siege, Spawn Control, Launch Race, Flag Chain, Armour Duel

column3: Audio Video Interleave video file; written only by the [B:DEBUG] grabber (`AVIGenerator`).

Bitmap pixel layouts found in the shipped `.bmp` files: 24-bit and 32-bit direct colour, 16- and 256-entry palettised, and run-length-encoded 8-bit (one file, which the decoder cannot read). All decode to RGBA8.
Byte-order mark; no shipped text file has one, and a UTF-8 BOM would be read as part of the first token.
Chinese, Japanese and Korean scripts; served by bitmap font atlases under `data/textures/unicode/`.
Computer-controlled team that fills an empty lobby slot (team type `TeamTypeCPU`), steered by an `AI` entity; also used for the processor in performance sections.

Cyclic redundancy check; a map's identity is the CRC-32 (reflected `0xEDB88320`, initial value 0, no final XOR) of its level-file bytes plus one `0xFF`, listed in `code/mapcrc.h` by the `tools/MapCRC` tool.
Line-ending conventions (carriage return plus line feed, or line feed only); the text reader accepts both.
The C run-time library (MSVC static multithreaded); its `rand()` and maths functions matter for determinism.
Comma-separated values; used for generated tables under `_work/drafts/`.
Capture the Statue, game type `GameTypeCaptureTheStatue`.
Direct3D, Microsoft's 3-D API; version 9 is the [B:D3D] back-end, D3DX its helper library.
Windows dynamic-link library (for example the delay-loaded `xinput1_3.dll`).
Digital signal processing; the audio filter chain configured by `effects.txt`, compiled but off in the shipped build (`USE_SOUND_DSPEFFECTS` commented out).

The time step of one simulation update: `SERVER_ADVANCE_PERIOD`, a macro for `0.1 × m_gameSpeed` game seconds (`GameTimer::GetServerAdvancePeriod`), applied once per tick to every slice-advanced object.
DirectX 12, the target graphics API of the new game.
Extended Backus-Naur form, the grammar notation used in 29.
Exponential moving average, as in fuel and power throughput smoothing `t = 0.8·t + 0.2·n`.
End of file.
End-user licence agreement (root `EULA.txt`); Introversion text, not to be reused.
First-in-first-out and last-in-first-out ordering, used when describing queues and lists.
Field of view of the camera projection.
Floating point, the floating-point unit, and the x87 instruction set the shipped Win32 build uses (53-bit precision control, no SSE2).
Frames per second (render rate), distinct from the 10 Hz simulation tick.
Full-scene and multisample anti-aliasing; the window can request multisampling, and a source comment ties the D3D deform path to FSAA.
File Transfer Protocol; the dead benchmark upload, and the name of the in-game `FTPManager` blob transfer over the letter channel.
Windows Vista Game Definition File compiled into the executable for Game Explorer ([B:DEAD] Vista integration).
OpenGL, the baseline renderer API (fixed-function pipeline, display lists).
The officer order (state `OrderGoto`) that turns an officer into a signpost redirecting idle Darwinians that pass within 100 wu toward the order point; sent as network command `ORDERGOTO` (`coa`).
Graphics processing unit.
High Level Shading Language; the 14 files in `data/shaders/` used only by the [B:D3D] path.
Health points, the unit of `m_stats[Health]` and of damage.
Heads-up display: the in-match overlay with scores, timers, task slots and messages.
Hardware 3-D sound mixing (DirectSound hardware buffers); an option exists but `USE_SOUND_HW3D` is off.
The floating-point standard; binary32 is single precision, to which every `iv_*` maths result is rounded.
Inverse kinematics; the two-bone leg solver of `EntityLeg`.
Input method editor for typing non-Latin text.
Key-value configuration file (`MultiwiniaSupport.ini`).
Internet Protocol address; the server stamps `FROMIP`/`FROMPORT` on every received letter.
Intellectual property; every Introversion name, text, art and audio asset is listed for replacement (see §3 and "IP items").
King of the Hill, game type `GameTypeKingOfTheHill`.
Local-area network (broadcast discovery on UDP 5009) and wide-area network (Internet play through the metaserver).
Linear congruential generator; the unsynced `AppRandom` family (`holdrand × 214013 + 2531011`) and the per-tile landscape generator use one.
Left and right mouse button.

Level of detail: frustum- and distance-based render simplification in about 73 world-object files; camera state reaches the simulation only through squad direct control and the blocked `ScriptTrigger`.
Least recently used, the eviction rule of the decoded-sample cache (above 60 MiB).
Gamepad left and right triggers and shoulder buttons (XInput).
Texture filter shorthand in asset tables: magnification and minification filters, `LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR` and `LINEAR`.
Message of the day, a text item fetched from the metaserver and shown in the main-menu information box.
Multiplayer and single-player. In code `App::Multiplayer()` is true for every Multiwinia match (including vs-CPU); SP branches are mostly Darwinia legacy.
Microsoft Visual C++ and Visual Studio 2005, the shipped toolchain (`targets/vs2005/`).
Mersenne Twister generator (Matsumoto–Nishimura); the algorithm behind the synced `syncrand` stream.

column3: Multiwinia, used as a prefix in tables and asset names (`mwhelp`, `mwsounds`, `mwtitle`).
Network address translation; the matchmaker helps peers behind NAT routers connect (hole punching).
Identifier of an unknown or design-critical inference in document NN (for example 05-U5), listed in that document's "Open questions and unknowns".
Non-power-of-two and power-of-two texture dimensions.
Windows installer generators; the Multiwinia installer scripts use Inno Setup (`tools/InstallerScript.iss`).
Operating system.
Identifiers of the analysis agents whose drafts were merged (partition agents, cross-cutting agents, synthesis agents); they appear in "Sources merged" headers and "Resolved:" notes.
Pulse-code modulation: uncompressed sample data delivered to the sound back-end.
Premium downloadable content; map ids 50–59 in `level_enum.txt` reserved for two absent map packs.
Portable Network Graphics; written for screenshots and thumbnails via libpng, never read as game data.
Atari sound chip whose envelope sequencer `EffectProcessor` emulates in the [B:DEBUG] sound editor; unrelated to `effects.txt` visuals.
Pipeline state object (Direct3D 12); the render-pass table in 24 is written so it maps onto a PSO catalogue.
`QueryPerformanceCounter`, the Win32 high-resolution clock behind `GetHighResTime`.
The archive format of the `.dat` data packs, read by the linked `contrib/unrar` library.
Colour channel orders; RGBA8 (8 bits per channel) is the in-memory format of every decoded bitmap.
Random number generator; synced (`syncrand` family, identical on all peers) versus unsynced (`AppRandom`, `frand`, CRT `rand`) generators are the key determinism distinction.
Real-time strategy, the genre.
Round-trip time of a network message.
Software development kit.
Simple DirectMedia Layer; used only by the Mac/Linux targets, [B:DEAD] on PC.
Windows structured exception handling; the crash handler writes `ERRORLOG.TXT` and `CRASH.DMP`.
Sequence id of a server letter (`NET_DARWINIA_SEQID`); clients execute letters strictly in sequence order, `−1` marks unsequenced letters.
Sound effects.
Hash function (from the bundled unrar sources) used for the server seed and the debug snapshot hash of an IFrame.
Stock-keeping unit: one retail edition of the product, chosen at data-build time (language set, exclusion list, distributor `origin` tag).
x86 SIMD instruction set; not enabled in the shipped build (`/arch:SSE2` absent).
Transport protocols; the game uses only UDP (game ports 4000/4001, metaserver 5113, LAN 5009).
Task manager, the slot list of granted powers.
Time to live (expiry of a cached server listing or packet).
User interface; user experience (tables use UX for a player-facing quirk).
Web address; store, metaserver and crash-report URLs are Introversion endpoints.

Unicode encodings. The non-English language tables are UTF-16 (big-endian for French, German, Italian, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish; little-endian for Japanese, Russian); preferences are saved as UTF-16LE.
Texture coordinates.
OpenGL vertex buffer object.
Visual effects: particles, beams, explosions, weather.
Windows virtual-key code.
Vertex shader and pixel shader (HLSL, [B:D3D]); also Visual Studio.
Uncompressed audio container, supported by the stream decoder alongside Ogg Vorbis.
Weapon of mass destruction: the player-facing name of the Assault pulse bomb.
World units, the length unit of the simulation (about one metre); speeds are wu per second.
Xbox Live Arcade; remnants of the console version (session pages, glyphs, `_xbox` phrase suffixes) are compiled out or unused on PC.
Microsoft gamepad API, delay-loaded from `xinput1_3.dll`; input driver 5.
Exclusive or (bitwise).

column1: # ---- Player concepts: modes and match framework ----

column3: Game type `GameTypeSkirmish` (enum 0): capture and hold spawn points; a team owning none for 30 consecutive mode seconds (after the first 30 game seconds) is eliminated; last team standing or best score at time-up wins.

Game type `GameTypeKingOfTheHill`: teams score for each hill zone in which they have the strictly largest Darwinian head count (recounted every game second); highest score at time-up wins; no elimination.
Game type `GameTypeCaptureTheStatue`: groups of Darwinians lift statues and carry them into their own drop zone; each delivery scores 1 point; highest score at time-up wins.

Game type `GameTypeAssault`: attackers must capture every control station linked to the defenders' pulse bomb before its countdown ends; if the countdown reaches zero the bomb detonates and the defenders win. Single round only in the shipped code.

Game type `GameTypeRocketRiot`: capture solar panels to power the fuel chain into your escape rocket, load 100 Darwinians at 95 % fuel, launch; the first rocket above world height y = 600 wins. No time limit, no draw.

Game type `GameTypeBlitzkreig` (sic): capture flag zones linked in a graph; a team is eliminated when an enemy captures its home flag while holding an unbroken chain of owned flags back to its own home flag. At time-up, flags held plus 10 per elimination decide.
Game type `GameTypeTankBattle`, compiled only with `INCLUDEGAMEMODE_TANKBATTLE` ([B:DEBUG]): each team has `NumTanks` tank lives; last team with tanks wins.

One of the seven `Multiwinia::GameType*` values (Skirmish = Domination, KingOfTheHill, CaptureTheStatue, Assault, RocketRiot, Blitzkreig, TankBattle); selects the per-mode `Advance*` rule function and the option blueprint in `data/multiwinia.txt`.
One played map from the end of loading to the results screen; the lifetime of a `Location` and of the per-match state.

The frozen pre-match phase (game speed 0) during which every human team must press Ready; once all are ready a 3-second countdown (`GRACE_TIME`) runs and un-readying restarts it. CPU teams are never waited for.
Per-team flag `Team::m_ready` toggled with Space or pad A during the grace period (network command `TOGGLE_READY`); in the lobby it toggles `LobbyTeam::m_ready`.
The 3-second "GAME STARTING IN" display at the end of the grace period, decremented 0.1 per tick with a tick sound per number and `CountdownZeroTick` at zero.
The unit of the per-mode rule clocks (time limit, reinforcement and elimination counters): one decrement every 11 ticks, so a displayed "second" lasts 1.1 game seconds.
Lobby option `TimeLimit` (mode minutes, 0 = unlimited) after which scores decide, or sudden death starts on a tie.
Per-slot integer `Multiwinia::m_score` whose meaning depends on the mode (zone seconds, statues delivered, flags held); the HUD shows it with the delta since the last mode second.

Once per mode second (not Assault, not Blitzkrieg) the local player gets a position message (phrases `dialog_position_<n>` or `dialog_tied_<n>`) whenever their rank among the non-special teams changes.

Two notions: the hard rules flag set by `Multiwinia::EliminateTeam` (Domination, Blitzkrieg, Tank Battle), and the soft `IsEliminated` query (KOTH, CTS: no spawn points and fewer than 50 Darwinians) that drives retribution. `Team::Eliminate` additionally kills the team's units.
Option `SuddenDeath`: on a tied score at time-up every team not on the top score is wiped and the next single leader wins; KOTH instead adds one-minute extensions.
A tied result at time-up with sudden death off; declared through `DeclareWinner` with no winning team.
The end-of-match sequence started by `Multiwinia::DeclareWinner`: scores are broadcast (and ignored by receivers), game speed is ramped to 0 and locked, and the winner and score overlay is shown.
HUD message `dialog_oneminute` shown once when the remaining time first drops to 60 mode seconds or less.
Comeback mechanism (option `RetributionMode`): every 45 s a team that `IsEliminated` receives random free powers, limited to 2 task slots while eliminated.
Lobby option (0–90 %, default 90) multiplying the spawn output of a team that owns fewer than two thirds of the other teams' average spawn points, by 1 + H/100 in every reachable case.
Option `StartingPowerups` (Domination, KOTH): 0–3 random powers granted to every team at match start.
Lobby check box (`multiwinia_param_basiccrates` → `Multiwinia::m_basicCratesOnly`, network option `GAMEOPTION_BASICCRATES`): only the 7 basic outcomes can be drawn and bad outcomes are disabled.
Two alliances of two players sharing a colour family, on maps whose options allow it; allied teams are friends for targeting and scoring.
A group of teams that `Location::IsFriend` treats as friendly (co-op pairs, Assault attacker or defender sides); not a separate object in the code.
The two sides of an Assault map: the level's `AttackingTeams` positions attack, the rest defend the pulse bomb.
One of eight colours (green, red, yellow, blue, orange, purple, cyan, pink) chosen in the lobby and applied to units, buildings and the HUD; co-op uses colour families.
The game-setup page (`PageGameSetup`) where the host picks map and options, players pick colour and side, CPU players fill slots and everyone readies up before start.
The host runs the `Server` and a `ClientToServer` in one process; every other player is a client of that server. All simulation runs on every client.
A connected participant without a team (team type `TeamTypeSpectator`); the dedicated spectator UI is [B:DEAD].
Joining a session already in progress: the client replays the server's entire letter history from sequence 0 to reconstruct the match.
Divergence of a client's simulation from its peers, detected by the per-frame sync byte; the affected client is reported out of sync and the game pauses for it, with no recovery.
Allowed only with no remote human players; ramps game speed to 0 over about 2 s (rate 0.2 per frame) and back.
`GameTimer::m_gameSpeed`, the multiplier on game time per tick (1 = normal); changed deterministically by pause, the Slow Down and Speed Up crates, meteor slow motion and the end of a match.
A level file `data/levels/mp_*.txt` named `mp_<mode>_<n>P_<k>` (57 Multiwinia maps, 49 in retail) defining terrain, buildings, starting units and mode options.
Per-level `MultiwiniaOptions` block: supported game types, player count, population cap, co-op flag, invalid crates, trunk-port settings and level options such as `instantspawnpointcapture`.

The lobby parameters of a mode defined in `data/multiwinia.txt` (39 definitions over 14 names: `ScoreMode`, `TimeLimit`, `Handicap`, `CrateDropRate`, `StartingPowerups`, `RetributionMode`, `SuddenDeath`, `CrateDropMode`, `ReinforcementTimer`, `ReinforcementCount`, `MaxArmour`, `TurretFrequency`, `MaxTurrets`, `NumTanks`), replicated to all peers.
Lobby option for CPU players (`Multiwinia::m_aiType` ∈ `AITypeEasy`, `AITypeStandard`, `AITypeHard`; shown as Easy, Normal, Hard); one setting for every CPU team.
The two live Multiwinia tutorials ("The Basics" on `mp_koth_2P_1`, "Advanced Concepts" on `mp_koth_3P_1`), driven by `MultiwiniaTutorial` with scripted CPU behaviour.
column5: yes → new tutorial maps and copy

column3: Contextual in-match hints (`MultiwiniaHelp`) that replace Darwinia's control-help system: short prompts about selection, promotion, crates and modes.
Front-end mode explainer animation played from a `.anim` script (`AnimatedPanel`), one per shipped mode.
One of 12 named goals evaluated by `AchievementTracker`; in the PC baseline unlocking is stubbed, so nothing is ever awarded.
The runtime-gated limited product (no valid full key): restricted maps and modes, enforced by `IS_DEMO` and the metaserver's demo limits.
The product key typed on `PageAuthKeyEntry`, checked locally and by the metaserver; decides full or demo status.
The LAN/WAN list of joinable games (`PageJoinGame`) filled from LAN broadcasts and metaserver listings.
Automatic match-finding page (`PageQuickMatchGame`), compiled but unreachable.
Seasonal theme negotiated in the lobby: snow weather, Santa hats on Darwinians and icy terrain ramps.
column5: yes → optional seasonal theme with new art

column3: Per-team limit on cap-counted bodies (`Team::m_others`) that freezes spawn-point and trunk-port production: the level's `PopulationCap` divided by the level's `NumPlayers` (Assault has separate attacker and defender caps).
The 30.0 s (300 ticks) after any ownership change before a spawn point produces; skipped for a team's only spawn point and on maps with `instantspawnpointcapture`.

The spawn-point request rhythm: while owned, activated and under the cap a point requests one virtual spirit every 0.2 s until it has requested `int(20 × handicap multiplier)` (20 without handicap), then pauses 10–15 s; the timer freezes while the cap is reached.

A `SpawnBuildingSpirit`: a token travelling along spawn links from the master spawn point to a requesting spawn point (1 s per link) that becomes one Darwinian on arrival; it has no position and cannot be intercepted.
The level's tree of master spawn point, spawn links and spawn points along which virtual spirits travel.
column5: yes → Source Node, Relays, Spawn Nodes

column3: A slot on a building, created from a `MarkerPort` shape marker, that one Darwinian occupies to operate or capture it; ports also carry per-team reservation counters.

Ownership change of a building by occupation or proximity. Each capturable type has its own rule and period (spawn point: a single team with at least 3 of 5 port occupants, re-evaluated every 2–3 s; gun turret 1 s; solar panel and control station every tick; zones and carryables 1 s).
The "no team" value of `WorldObjectId::m_teamId`; neutral buildings can be captured, neutral spawn points produce nothing.
One of `NUM_TEAMS` = 6 team indices: 0–3 players, 4 the monster team, 5 the Futurewinian team; 255 = none.
The circle grown by holding the left button (up to 100 wu) that selects Darwinians for a crowd order (`Location::SelectDarwinians`).
A move order given to the selected Darwinians (command `ORDERDGS`): they walk to the point as a loose group, optionally by direct route.
Turning a selected Darwinian into an officer (command `PROMOTE`) and back; officers are created only this way.
A block of up to 90 Darwinians marching in rows of 6 to 15 in front of an officer, which fight as one; set with the officer's formation order.
Steering a single unit or building yourself (squad, armour, harvester, engineer, gun turret aim, radar dish aim) through the continuous `TeamControls` packet.
A granted ability (unit, strike, turret, buff) held by the `TaskManager` until the player places it on the map; called "program" in the Darwinia fiction.
One of the 6 task-manager slots (2 while eliminated); a full manager rejects new grants with "Powerup Limit Reached!".

Every opened crate resolves once: with probability 0.9 a good outcome for the opening team (`Crate::CaptureCrate`, uniform over the valid good types), otherwise a bad outcome (`Crate::RunUncapturedCrate`) created for the monster team (Space Ship: the Futurewinian team). Basic-crates-only games always take the good branch.
Timed waves from owned trunk ports: every 60 mode seconds each owned port emits Darwinians and, per mode, armour, turret or air-strike tasks ("Reinforcements in *S").
Forces present at match start: the level's `InstantUnits` plus 5 Darwinians seeded on every port of every team-owned spawn point and solar panel.
Collection of floating spirits of any team by a Harvester, which turns each into a Darwinian of its own team at a friendly spawn point, bypassing the population cap.
A KOTH `MultiwiniaZone` ring that scores for the team with the most Darwinians inside it.
CTS `MultiwiniaZone`s: team-owned zones that score delivered statues, and neutral zones where new statues appear.
A Blitzkrieg `MultiwiniaZone` captured by Darwinian majority; zones are linked into a graph, and a home flag is each team's base.
`Statue` (CarryableBuilding), created at run time in CTS only: a relic lifted by enough Darwinians and carried; delivered within 30 wu of an owned drop zone it scores 1 point.
Pressure passed down the chain solar panel → power line → fuel generator → pipes → fuel station → escape rocket; the rocket needs 95 % to load passengers.
The 100 Darwinians that must board an escape rocket through its fuel station before launch.
Team slot 4, a CPU faction ("Evilinians") that owns every bad crate outcome, ant hills, triffids and infected units, and can even win KOTH on score.
Team slot 5, the faction dropped by the Space Ship outcome; its Darwinians use the `futurewinian.bmp` sprite.
Scenery `Tree` buildings: flammable, regrowing, blocking; Magical Forest trees drop spirits, Dark Forest ("evil") trees kill Darwinians and corrupt neighbours.
`g_app->m_camera` (`code/camera.cpp`): 15 camera modes, of which free movement (the match camera), entity tracking and building aim are live in Multiwinia.

`Crate` (Building): a falling bubble-wrapped box dropped every `CrateDropRate` seconds; the team holding the strict Darwinian majority within 35 wu (`CRATE_SCAN_RANGE`) opens it; a crate left neutral on the ground for 60 s expires with no effect.
`Crate::CrateReward*`, 31 outcomes in FULL (indices 0–30) plus The Beast (31) in DEBUG; `NumCrateRewards` sizes the per-level invalid-crate table.
Lobby options `CrateDropRate` (seconds between drops, 0 = none, default 40) and `CrateDropMode` (Random or Weighted placement).
Level-file `InvalidCrates` list of outcome names excluded from the draws on that map.
Outcome 0 `CrateRewardSquad` (basic): a placed task spawning a 3-man insertion squad that lives 60 s.
Outcome 1 `CrateRewardHarvester` (advanced, needs spawn points): a placed flying spirit collector.
Outcome 2 `CrateRewardEngineer` (basic, needs spawn points): a placed hovering spirit collector.
Outcome 3 `CrateRewardArmour` (basic; invalid in Rocket Riot and where `trunkportarmour` is set): a placed troop transport.
Outcome 4 `CrateRewardAirstrike` (basic): 3–7 smoke markers each summon 2 bombers that drop one bomb (explosion radius 25, damage 100).

Outcome 5 `CrateRewardNuke` (advanced): 10 submarine-launched warheads at the target (radius 50, damage 100 each), the first exactly on the point and nine within ±150; needs sea on the map. Each warhead is entity type 21 `Nuke`.

column3: The process-wide application object (`code/app.h`), reached through the global `g_app`; owns every subsystem pointer (renderer, sound, network, location, menus) and the game-mode state.
`App::m_gameMode` ∈ {GameModeNone, GameModePrologue, GameModeCampaign, GameModeMultiwinia}; only Multiwinia is reachable in FULL.

The match world (`code/location.h`, `g_app->m_location`): teams, buildings, spirits, lasers, effects, landscape, water, grids, routing; advances the simulation in slices and resolves `WorldObjectId`s.
`g_app->m_multiwinia` (`code/multiwinia.h`): game type, options, lobby teams, grace period, per-mode `Advance*` rules, trunk ports, retribution, scores, HUD and `DeclareWinner`.
Darwinia's world-map object; in Multiwinia only a holder of the local team id and research levels ([B:LEGACY] otherwise).
The research table (`GlobalResearch::Type*`, one level per type); fixed in Multiwinia, its type ids double as task types.
Per-match team container (`code/team.h`, `Location::m_teams[6]`): units, `m_others`, task manager, selection, colour and team type, bound by reference to its `LobbyTeam`.
Persistent per-slot roster record in `Multiwinia::m_teams[6]` (id, client, type, colour, ready flag) that survives lobby, match and results.
`Team::m_teamType`: Unused (−1), LocalPlayer (0), RemotePlayer (1), CPU (2), Spectator (3).
The team's loose entity list (`Team::m_others`, unit id −1): Darwinians, officers, armour and other bodies; it is what the population cap counts.
`code/unit.h:Unit`: a team-owned group of same-type entities moving together (insertion squads, bomber flights, Virii groups, centipede segments, instant units).
Negative `WorldObjectId::m_unitId` values selecting a non-team container: `UNIT_BUILDINGS` −100, `UNIT_SPIRITS` −101, `UNIT_LASERS` −102, `UNIT_EFFECTS` −103.
`#define` 6 in `code/globals.h`: four player slots plus the monster and Futurewinian teams.
One tenth of a simulation tick: every slice-partitioned container advances about a tenth of its slots per slice (`NUM_SLICES_PER_FRAME` = 10), so each object advances exactly once per tick.
One simulation step = one server UPDATE letter, produced every 0.1 s of real time (10 Hz) and advancing game time by `0.1 × game speed`.
`g_predictionTime`: the render-time extrapolation of positions since the last tick (no interpolation); render-only.
Network-safe game clock (`code/gametimer.h`): game time, game speed with requested blends, `SERVER_ADVANCE_PERIOD`, `GetNetworkTime`.
Macro for `g_gameTimer.GetServerAdvancePeriod()` = `0.1 × m_gameSpeed`: the dt of one tick.
Game time (`GameTimer::GetGameTime`, deterministic) versus wall-clock time (`GetHighResTime`, QPC-based, not deterministic).
Per-team uniform grid of entity ids (32 wu cells) kept up to date as entities move; answers neighbour and enemy-count queries. The cache memoises repeated queries within a tick.
Spatial index of buildings: each world cell lists the unique ids of the buildings overlapping it; used for obstacle pushes and placement tests.
Path-finding: a waypoint graph over walkable land built at load (`LandRoutingSystem::Initialise`) and route generation between points.
A generated path (list of waypoints) held in a slot-shared array; a unit follows it point by point.
The continuous per-team input packet (cursor world position, button states, unit-control flags) packed into `ALIVE_DATA` every frame and executed by `Location::UpdateTeam`.
Per-team container of granted powers (`code/taskmanager.h`): 6 slots in multiplayer; each `Task` moves through Idle, Started (waiting to be placed), Running and Stopping.
The live task-bar interface: power slots at the screen edge, the running-task bar and the "power-up received" pop-up.

Level-file `InstantUnits` rows `type team x z count inAUnit state spread [waypoint [route [runAsTask]]]` placing starting entities for the team at that start position; 16 blocked entity types are refused.
Level-file block of Darwinia tasks that start with the level ([B:LEGACY]).
A building or entity type that `BuildingIsBlocked` / `EntityIsBlocked` refuse to place from level files under `BLOCK_OLD_DARWINIA_OBJECTS`.
Named point inside a `.shp` mesh (for example `MarkerPort01`, `MarkerDoor`, `MarkerSpiritLink`) that code looks up to place ports, doors, beams and effects.
The determinism boundary: state that must evolve identically on all peers (positions, health, synced RNG) versus render-only state (particles, prediction, sound).

`g_app->m_server` (`code/network/server.cpp`), present only on the host: accepts clients, assigns team slots, sequences and broadcasts commands at 10 Hz, keeps the full history, compares sync bytes and advertises the game.
`g_app->m_clientToServer`: every peer's client side; sends requests and `ALIVE` input, receives letters, executes them in sequence order and produces the sync byte.
One server-to-client message (`code/network/servertoclientletter.h`): receiver id, disconnect flag and a `Directory` payload; UPDATE letters carry one tick's commands.
The per-tick server letter carrying every command of that tick in order; exactly one per tick even if empty, numbered by sequence id.
The network model: all peers run the full simulation from identical ordered command streams and a shared RNG seed; only inputs travel, never state.
`code/network/iframe.cpp`: produces the per-frame sync byte (in FULL the next synced-RNG draw, `255 × syncfrand(1)`); in debug and beta builds a SHA-1 world snapshot that can be diffed.
The one byte per frame each client sends so the server can detect divergence; in FULL it only reveals divergence of the synced RNG stream position.
SystemIV registry-like container (`contrib/systemiv/lib/tosser/directory.h`): a named node with typed named fields and child nodes, serialised to bytes; every network and metaserver message is one.
SystemIV's "very thin portable UDP network library" (`contrib/systemiv/lib/netlib`): sockets, listener threads, `NetMutex`, `NetEvent`, `NetStartThread`.
NetLib's portable mutex, event and thread wrappers (Win32 critical sections, events and `CreateThread`).
Binding between a lobby UI control and a replicated game option (`code/network/networkvalue.*`); floats travel as `%.2f` text.
Per-link byte-rate statistics, and a [B:DEAD] link simulator (latency, loss, bandwidth) for testing.
Reliable blob transfer over the letter channel (`FILESEND` letters); in the baseline it only moves IFrame sync snapshots between client and server after a desync.
`code/network/demo_limitations.*`: limits on what a demo client may host or join, filled from the metaserver data item `Demo2Limits` or built-in defaults.

Introversion's external Internet server directory (`contrib/systemiv/lib/metaserver`, UDP 5113): server registration and listing, key authentication, MOTD, latest version and demo limits. Its server side is not in the tree.
The metaserver component that helps peers behind NAT reach each other (hole-punching requests) before a join.

Broadcast of hosted games on the local network (UDP 5009) for the server browser.
The deterministic MT19937 stream shared by all peers (`contrib/systemiv/lib/math/random_number.*`), seeded per session by the server; `syncfrand(r)` ∈ [0, r), `syncsfrand(r)` ∈ [−r/2, r/2).
Marker macros that draw synced random vector components in a fixed x, y, z order inside `Vector3` constructors, avoiding unspecified argument evaluation order.
The unsynced LCG family (MSVC `rand()` clone, seeded 1 per level): for cosmetics only, though trees misuse it.

Maths wrappers (`iv_sin`, `iv_cos`, `iv_tan`, `iv_asin`, `iv_acos`, `iv_atan`, `iv_sqrt`, `iv_pow`, `iv_exp`, `iv_log`, plus parsing helpers such as `iv_atof`) that round each CRT result to IEEE binary32 with `iv_trunc_low_nibble` to keep peers bit-identical.
Files `syncerror-…` and `syncdiff-…` written on a sync error for forensics.

Introversion's shared utility library (`contrib/systemiv`): in Multiwinia only containers (tosser), NetLib, metaserver, maths and RNG, file readers, Unicode strings, debug utilities and the profiler are compiled.
SystemIV's container sub-library (`contrib/systemiv/lib/tosser`): `LList`, `DArray`, `FastDArray`, `BTree`, `HashTable`, `Directory`.
SystemIV doubly linked list with a cached cursor (so even reads mutate state and need a lock across threads).
SystemIV dynamic array with per-slot used flags: an entry's index never changes and freed slots are reused.
`DArray` with a free list, so insertion is O(1); used for entities, effects and spirits.
`FastDArray` that also hands out per-slice index ranges (`GetNextSliceBounds`) so a loop over all members can be spread across the 10 slices of a tick (`code/lib/slice_darray.h`).
SystemIV binary tree keyed by string ids (sorted, fast look-up); used for example by the phrase table `LangTable`.
SystemIV string-keyed hash table (used for example by the FTP manager's transfer lists).
Template 2-D arrays over the world (`code/lib/2d_array.*`, `2d_surface_map.*`) used for height maps and grids.
Double-precision maths types of `code/lib`; a second SystemIV `Vector3` coexists.
SystemIV wide string; single-byte text is widened byte-for-byte (ISO-8859-1).
Line reader and tokeniser shared by every text format (comments, separators, `redshirt2` detection); implemented by text-file and Unicode-file readers.
Reader for binary resources (archives, bitmaps, Ogg files).
The linked `contrib/unrar` library that opens `.dat` archives into memory-mapped files; not thread-safe, which serialises sound loading.
SystemIV archive-aware file system: compiled but unused.

SystemIV section profiler (`contrib/systemiv/lib/profiler`) displayed in the profiler window.
